note: The client's claim about itself: which error codes it can mint without reading one from the edge's body (`mintedByClient`) and which it only ever recognises from a body (`recognisedFromServer`). The halves are declared here, not derived from the code — CloudContractCodeCheckTest checks membership against CloudRouteErrorCodes.KNOWN, so a code added or removed without this file fails the test, while which half a code sits in does not. What the socket path mints, and why: a missing or blank token yields unauthorized (CloudTurnRoute); a failed socket yields connection_lost via the transport's onFailure callback; a text frame that does not decode yields invalid_response; and a socket the server closes itself (onClosed) closes the route's flow with NO error event at all, so the turn returns Silent — the user hears nothing rather than an error, which is worth knowing before reading that path as an error. invalid_request and internal_error are declared as client-mintable but nothing in the tree mints them today — no bare 4xx or thrown stream produces them since the client moved to the single socket transport — so treat those two as spec-defined rather than verified by code. specRevision is the revision of the spec table this claim was last checked against; bumping it is a deliberate act, not a side effect of an edit.
